meeting_date.text: November 19, 2008 (an earlier meeting scheduled for February 27, 2008 was cancelled days before, pending evaluation of inspectional findings)

quote.quote: Telavancin was presented to the Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee meeting on November 19, 2008.

recommendation.text: The Committee voted 21 Yes to 5 No that the safety and effectiveness of telavancin for cSSSI had been demonstrated; it also recommended labeling on QT interval, renal toxicity, and teratogenic effects, and voted 25 Yes to 1 No that a risk management strategy was needed to prevent unintended use in pregnant women.

quote.quote: The Committee voted that the safety and effectiveness of telavancin for the treatment of cSSSI had been demonstrated (Yes: 21, No 5).

linkages.concern: The Committee voted 25 Yes to 1 No that a risk management strategy was needed to prevent unintended use of telavancin in pregnant women, and described elements to consider in a program to manage risks.
linkages.change: The approval includes a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) with a Medication Guide, a communication plan (Dear Healthcare Provider letters), and a timeline for assessments; the Office Director states this risk-management program is consistent with the Advisory Committee's recommendations.

concern_quote.quote: The Committee also voted Yes 25, No 1, on the question of whether a risk management strategy was needed to prevent unintended use in pregnant women and described elements to consider in a program to manage risks.

change_quote.quote: Development of a program to manage the risks of telavancin is also consistent with the recommendations of the Advisory Committee.

linkages.concern: The Committee recommended that the product labeling include information regarding teratogenic effects.
linkages.change: The product labeling includes a boxed warning regarding fetal risk, accompanied by a Medication Guide.

concern_quote.quote: The Committee also recommended that the product labeling include information regarding the effect on the QT interval, renal toxicity, and teratogenic effects.

change_quote.quote: The product labeling, which includes a boxed warning regarding fetal risk, and the Medication Guide provide information describing the risks of telavancin.

linkages.concern: The Committee recommended that the product labeling include information regarding renal toxicity.
linkages.change: Information on renal adverse events, including a nephrotoxicity warning, was incorporated into the product labeling.

concern_quote.quote: The Committee also recommended that the product labeling include information regarding the effect on the QT interval, renal toxicity, and teratogenic effects.

change_quote.quote: Information on renal adverse events has been incorporated in the product labeling, including a warning on nephrotoxicity.

linkages.concern: The Committee recommended that the product labeling include information regarding the effect on the QT interval.
linkages.change: The approved label includes a QTc Prolongation warning (Section 5.8) advising caution and avoidance of use in patients at risk.

concern_quote.quote: The Committee also recommended that the product labeling include information regarding the effect on the QT interval, renal toxicity, and teratogenic effects.

change_quote.quote: Caution is warranted when prescribing VIBATIV to patients taking drugs known to prolong the QT interval.

summary: An Anti-Infective Drugs Advisory Committee meeting was held on November 19, 2008 (an earlier February 27, 2008 meeting was cancelled over clinical-site inspectional findings), where the committee voted 21-5 that telavancin's safety and effectiveness for cSSSI were demonstrated. The committee recommended labeling on QT interval, renal toxicity, and teratogenic effects, and voted 25-1 that a risk-management strategy was needed to prevent unintended use in pregnant women. The approval incorporated these inputs: a REMS with a Medication Guide (which the Office Director states is consistent with the committee's recommendations), a boxed warning on fetal risk, a nephrotoxicity warning, and a QTc prolongation warning.
